# Slurmtools for submitting NONMEM runs

`slurmtools` is an R package for interacting with slurm (fka **S**imple **L**inux **U**tility for **R**esource **M**anagement) and submitting NONMEM jobs. You can submit a NONMEM job with `submit_slurm_job`, you can view current jobs with `get_slurm_jobs`, and you can see the available partitions with `get_slurm_partitions`.

## Installing `slurmtools`

To install `slurmtools` use the following commands:

```{r setup}
library(slurmtools)
```

We are given a message when loading slurmtools that some options are not set and that default job submission will not work without them. These options are used for default arguments in the `submit_slurm_job` function. Running `?submit_slurm_job` we can see the documentation

## Default variables and values provided to the template

This function uses the inputs to populate a template Bash shell script that submits the NONMEM job to slurm. Default templates ship with the package in `system.file("templates", package = "slurmtools")`, and you can supply your own via the `template` argument to do additional tasks as long as they are possible within Bash.

By default these values are provided to the slurm template file:

-   `partition` is an argument to `submit_slurm_job` by default this will be the first element of `get_slurm_partitions()`

-   `parallel` is `TRUE` if `ncpu > 1`, else `FALSE`

-   `ncpu` is an argument to `submit_slurm_job` - your input of `ncpu` must be less than or equal to the number of cpus on the `partition`

-   `num_mpi_cpus` mirrors `ncpu`

-   `job_name` is created from the `input` argument supplied to `submit_slurm_job` - for a NONMEM model it is `<nonmem_model_name>-nonmem-run`

-   `account` is an argument to `submit_slurm_job` (`--account`); it is omitted from the script when `NULL`

-   `log_path` is `<submission_root>/<job_name>.out`

-   `model_path` is determined from the `input` argument supplied to `submit_slurm_job`

-   `config_path` is determined via `getOption("slurmtools.config_path")`, or the `config_path` argument

-   `bbi_exe_path` is the absolute path to `bbi`, resolved at submit time via `Sys.which("bbi")` so the rendered script names the exact binary that will run. Submission errors early if `bbi` cannot be found; point at a specific binary with `template_opts = list(bbi_exe_path = "/path/to/bbi")`

If you need to feed more arguments to the template you simply supply them in the `template_opts` argument as a list. More on that later.

``` r
default_template_list = list(
  job_name = sprintf("%s-nonmem-run", basename(input$absolute_model_path)),
  partition = partition,
  ncpu = ncpu,
  parallel = ncpu > 1,
  num_mpi_cpus = ncpu,
  account = account,
  log_path = file.path(submission_root, sprintf("%s.out", job_name)),
  model_path = input$absolute_model_path,
  config_path = config_path,
  bbi_exe_path = Sys.which("bbi")
)
```

## Submitting a NONMEM job with `bbi`

To submit a NONMEM job, we create a model object from `bbr` and pass it as the `input` to `submit_slurm_job`. A shipped `nonmem-bbi` template is used by default, or you can supply your own with the `template` argument. To use `bbi` we also need a `bbi.yaml` file, which I've also supplied in `/model/nonmem/bbi.yaml` (and is also supplied with the R project starter).

Here is an example of a template file that will call `bbi`:

``` slurm-job-bbi.tmpl
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name="{{job_name}}"
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task={{ncpu}}
#SBATCH --partition={{partition}}
{{#account}}
#SBATCH --account={{account}}
{{/account}}
#SBATCH --output={{log_path}}

# submit_slurm_job uses the whisker package to populate template files
# https://github.com/edwindj/whisker

{{#parallel}}
bbi nonmem run local {{model_path}}.mod --parallel --threads={{ncpu}} --config {{config_path}}
{{/parallel}}


{{^parallel}}
bbi nonmem run local {{model_path}}.mod --config {{config_path}}
{{/parallel}}
```

This file will call `bbi` to run our supplied model (`{{model_path}}.mod`) if `ncpu > 1` then parallel will be true and the code between `{{#parallel}}` and `{{/parallel}}` will be populated. if `ncpu = 1` then parallel will be false and the code between `{{^parallel}}` and `{{/parallel}}` will be populated. The command lives in the template, so `bbi` needs to be on the path of the compute node (or the template edited to point at it).

```{r}
Sys.which("bbi")
```

We will use a few different template files with different functionality so we'll inject those template file paths to `submit_slurm_job`. However, we'll use the `submission-log` directory for the output, so we'll set that option as well as `slurmtools.config_path` so `submit_slurm_job` defaults can be used. The slurm template files are saved in `~/model/nonmem/` Additionally, there is a simple NONMEM control stream in `1001.mod` in the same directory that we can use for testing.

```{r}
library(bbr)
library(here)

nonmem = file.path(here::here(), "vignettes", "model", "nonmem")

options('slurmtools.submission_root' = file.path(nonmem, "submission-log"))
options('slurmtools.config_path' = file.path(nonmem, "bbi.yaml"))
```

To create the `bbr` model object, we need to have both `1001.mod` and `1001.yaml` which contains metadata about the model in the supplied directory (`./model/nonmem/`). We'll check for mod_number.yaml and if it exists, read in the model otherwise create it and then read it.

```{r}
mod_number <- "1001"

if (file.exists(file.path(nonmem, paste0(mod_number, ".yaml")))) {
  mod <- bbr::read_model(file.path(nonmem, mod_number))
} else {
  mod <- bbr::new_model(file.path(nonmem, mod_number))
}
```

We can now submit the job and point to the template file in `model/nonmem/slurm-job-bbi.tmpl`.

```{r}
submission <- slurmtools::submit_slurm_job(
  mod,
  overwrite = TRUE,
  template = file.path(nonmem, "slurm-job-bbi.tmpl"),
)

submission
```

We see a `status` with an exit code of 0 suggesting a successful command, and the `stdout` gives us the batch job number. We can use `slurmtools::get_slurm_jobs()` to monitor the status of the job. Here, we can supply the `user` argument to filter to just the jobs we've submitted.

```{r}
slurmtools::get_slurm_jobs(user = Sys.info()[["user"]])
```

If we look in the `slurmtools.submisstion_root` directory we can see the shell script that was generated with `submit_slurm_job`. Here is the whisker replaced call to bbi:

``` 1001.sh
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name="1001-nonmem-run"
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH --partition=cpu2mem4gb
#SBATCH --output=/data/user-homes/tariq/projects/slurmtools/vignettes/model/nonmem/submission-log/1001-nonmem-run.out

# submit_slurm_job uses the whisker package to populate template files
# https://github.com/edwindj/whisker

bbi nonmem run local /data/user-homes/tariq/projects/slurmtools/vignettes/model/nonmem/1001.mod --config /data/user-homes/tariq/projects/slurmtools/vignettes/model/nonmem/bbi.yaml
```

## Extending templates

Because the templates create a bash shell script there is an almost infinite number of things we can do with our template. **Anything you can do in bash you can do by appropriately updating the template file and injecting the needed information!**

Let's add a notification feature that will send a notification when the job has started and finished. We can use [ntfy.sh](ntfy.sh) and add the necessary info to our template to achieve this.

Here is a modified template file that adds a `JOBID=$SLURM_JOBID` and some ntfy calls. To get a notification we can supply `submit_slurm_job` with an `ntfy` variable via `template_opts`. I'll use `ntfy = "ntfy_demo"` for this.

``` slurm-job-bbi-ntfy.tmpl
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name="{{job_name}}"
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task={{ncpu}}
#SBATCH --partition={{partition}}
{{#account}}
#SBATCH --account={{account}}
{{/account}}
#SBATCH --output={{log_path}}

JOBID=$SLURM_JOBID

# submit_slurm_job uses the whisker package to populate template files
# https://github.com/edwindj/whisker

{{#ntfy}}
curl -d "Starting model run: {{job_name}} $JOBID" ntfy.sh/{{ntfy}}
{{/ntfy}}

{{#parallel}}
bbi nonmem run local {{model_path}}.mod --parallel --threads={{ncpu}} --config {{config_path}}
{{/parallel}}

{{^parallel}}
bbi nonmem run local {{model_path}}.mod --config {{config_path}}
{{/parallel}}

{{#ntfy}}
curl -d "Finished model run: {{job_name}} $JOBID" ntfy.sh/{{ntfy}}
{{/ntfy}}
```

Since we've already run this model we will provide the `overwrite = TRUE` argument to force a new nonmem run.

```{r}
submission_ntfy <- slurmtools::submit_slurm_job(
  mod,
  template = file.path(nonmem, "slurm-job-bbi-ntfy.tmpl"),
  overwrite = TRUE,
  template_opts = list(
    ntfy = "ntfy_demo")
)

submission_ntfy
```

We again get a 0 exit code status and now instead of using `slurmtools::get_slurm_jobs()` to monitor the job, we can rely on the new notifications we just set up. ![NONMEM job starting ntfy alert](data/images/ntfy_starting.png)

and when the run finished we get another notification: ![NONMEM Job finished ntfy alert](data/images/ntfy_finished.png)

Note that the run number will match the run specified in `submission$stdout`. We can see the new shell script this updated template file generated

``` 1001.sh
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name="1001-nonmem-run"
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH --partition=cpu2mem4gb
#SBATCH --output=/data/user-homes/tariq/projects/slurmtools/vignettes/model/nonmem/submission-log/1001-nonmem-run.out

JOBID=$SLURM_JOBID

curl -d "Starting model run: 1001-nonmem-run $JOBID" ntfy.sh/ntfy_demo

bbi nonmem run local /data/user-homes/tariq/projects/slurmtools/vignettes/model/nonmem/1001.mod --config /data/user-homes/tariq/projects/slurmtools/vignettes/model/nonmem/bbi.yaml

curl -d "Finished model run: 1001-nonmem-run $JOBID" ntfy.sh/ntfy_demo
```

To reiterate, this template file is run as a bash shell script so anything you can do in bash you can put into the template and pass the needed arguments and customize the behavior to your liking.

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
# cancelling the nonmem jobs submitted above (and only those)
jobs <- vapply(
  list(submission, submission_ntfy),
  function(sub) as.numeric(gsub("\\D", "", sub$stdout)),
  numeric(1)
)

for (job in jobs) {
  tryCatch({
    cancel_slurm_job(job, auto_confirm = TRUE)
  }, error = function(e) {}
  )
}

unlink(file.path(nonmem, "1001"), recursive = TRUE)
unlink(file.path(nonmem, "1001.yaml"))
unlink(file.path(nonmem, "submission-log"), recursive = TRUE)
unlink(file.path(nonmem, "in_progress"), recursive = TRUE)
```
